scope: Nodes 1..N; MaxReads read operations. Normal cases use logs of at most 4 entries, with two terms (default) or three (three_terms). xfer_read_no_record_lag keeps the earlier bound of two terms and 5 entries; it records applied together with the apply. Deadlock checking is off and liveness is not claimed.

RecordLag multiplies the state space about 7 times (30,344,221 vs 4,550,621 distinct states at the default bound), so the 5-entry bound is checked only without it. Without xfer reads, the lag only delays what followers learn and when reads finish, so it should add no behavior that breaks Linearizable; TLC does not check this argument.

Replication is one global log of entries that are or will be committed. Uncommitted entries that a later leader discards are omitted: no node applies them and their writes never respond, so reads cannot observe them.
Every node holds the whole global log; a node applies up to `known`, the bound learned from a leader. Real replication lag only removes behaviors.

Learn reads the current leader's advertised bound at send time. Delayed or stale AppendEntries are covered because `known` only grows, applying is a separate step, and a stale leader's bound is below the current no-op.
Only the latest elected leader appends and commits. Commit through k requires k >= the term's no-op index (the current-term commit rule).

Read authorization is atomic and requires the reading leader to be the latest elected leader. This stands for a ReadIndex quorum confirmation or a valid lease, both of which rule out a higher-term leader at that point.

Read invocation is merged into authorization, and the response into the query sample. Both make `floor` at least as large as in a real execution, so a pass covers later invocations and later responses.
A read's state is the applied prefix of one node; the property compares the number of writes in prefixes of the committed log.

`applied` means visible to fresh state-machine queries; `recorded` is the applied index RaftCore has recorded, published as metrics.last_applied and advertised to followers. With RecordLag, a write can respond, and a query can see it, before it is recorded. RespondAfterApply=false lets a write respond once committed, before its proposer's state includes it.

Snapshot installation is not a separate action. A snapshot holds at most the leader's applied prefix, which Learn plus Apply reach with an equal or larger bound in both advertising modes. Crash, restart and log purge are not modeled.
With Validate, a relaxed read rejects a sampled entry whose term differs from the authorizing term; no retry is modeled. This is the design of PR revision 9df30829; the bound revision removed it.

A relaxed linearizer awaited on a node other than the one that issued it waits for max(noop, committed) (LinearizeState::read_log_id_on), which is the std read on that node; relaxed reads are therefore modeled only on the issuing node.
A finished read keeps only whether it satisfied Linearizable and a witness tag; a write response only raises doneFloor. Neither affects later behavior.
Read ids are interchangeable, so reads start in id order (symmetry breaking).

audit: Witness NeverStaleNextTermRelaxed first matched a node re-elected in the next term, not a stepped-down node. Tightened it to a relaxed read finishing on a node that is no longer leader and returning a write of a later leadership.

The first version applied and recorded an entry in one step, so the xfer barrier max(noop, leader applied) passed. ApplyResponder::send responds inside apply(), before RaftCore records the entry; splitting Record from Apply makes the xfer read violate Linearizable.
